Meta.title: Ausculta: health information that listens
Meta.description: Ask about a condition, a test or a medicine. Plain-language answers from public health sources, each one cited.

Common.tagline: Health information that listens, and shows its sources.

Landing.heroTitle: Health information that listens, and shows its sources.
Landing.heroSubtitle: Ask about a condition, a test or a medicine. Plain-language answers from public health sources, each one cited.
Landing.previewQuestion: What does an HbA1c test measure?
Landing.previewAnswer: An HbA1c test measures your average blood sugar level over the past three months [1]. It is used to check for diabetes and to see how well diabetes is managed over time [1].
Landing.previewSeekCare: Your doctor can explain what your own result means.
Landing.previewSourcePublisher: MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine
Landing.previewSourceSnippet: A hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) test is a blood test that shows what your average blood sugar (glucose) level was over the past three months.
Landing.previewCaption: Example answer. Every source opens on the publisher’s own site.
Landing.howIntro: Four things happen between your question and the answer, in this order.

listen.title: Listens
listen.body: Write in English, French or Arabic. Names, phone numbers and other personal details are removed before anything else happens.

check.title: Checks for urgency first
check.body: Every message is checked for signs of an emergency or a crisis. If there is one, you see emergency contacts straight away, before any other answer.

search.title: Searches trusted sources
search.body: Ausculta looks only in a licence-checked library of public health sources. If it finds nothing reliable, it tells you instead of guessing.

answer.title: Answers with citations
answer.body: Each statement points to its source and the date the source was reviewed. Answers about medicines are checked against their sources before you see them.

Landing.safetyTitle: Clear about what it will not do
Landing.safetyIntro: Ausculta explains general health information. Decisions about your health belong with you and your care team.

never.diagnose: Tell you what condition you have
never.triage: Decide how urgent your situation is
never.dose: Give you a personal dose or change your treatment
never.replace: Replace a doctor, nurse or pharmacist

always.cite: Show where each answer comes from
always.seekCare: Tell you when to seek care
always.human: Keep a person at the hospital one tap away
always.unknown: Say so when it does not know
always.label: Make clear you are talking to an AI assistant

Landing.sourcesBody: Answers come only from public health publishers whose licences allow reuse. Each source is listed with its licence, so you can read the original.
Landing.deskBody: Practical questions about the hospital are answered from information the hospital has verified, never from the AI’s imagination.

hours.title: Opening hours and directions
hours.body: When departments are open and how to find them.

departments.title: Departments and contacts
departments.body: Who to call, and where each service is.

visiting.title: Visiting rules
visiting.body: Visiting times and what to bring for a stay.

appointment.title: Appointment requests
appointment.body: A simple form sends your request to hospital staff. What you enter in it is never shared with the AI.

doctor.a: No. It is an AI assistant that explains general health information from public sources. It cannot examine you, diagnose you or decide what you should do. For that, talk to a doctor, nurse or pharmacist.

sources.q: Where do the answers come from?
sources.a: From a library of public health sources whose licences allow reuse, such as MedlinePlus. Each answer cites its sources, and you can open them to read the original.

privacy.q: What happens to what I type?
privacy.a: Names, phone numbers and other identifiers are removed before your message is processed. Conversations are not stored by default. Appointment requests go only to hospital staff.

emergency.q: What if it is an emergency?
emergency.a: Ausculta is not an emergency service. If you think someone’s life is in danger, call your local emergency number now. If you mention an emergency, Ausculta shows emergency contacts first.

languages.a: English, French and Arabic. Many sources are written in English; when an answer relies on them, Ausculta tells you.

unknown.q: Why does it sometimes say it does not know?
unknown.a: When its sources do not cover a question well enough, Ausculta says so rather than guess. You can then ask a clinician or the front desk.

Footer.disclaimer: Ausculta gives general health information and helps you find your way around the hospital. It does not diagnose, assess urgency or prescribe, and it is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
Footer.demo: Demo version. Not for use with real patients.
Footer.attribution: Health content is credited to its publishers on the Sources page.

About.title: About Ausculta
About.lead: Ausculta is an AI assistant for general health information and hospital navigation. Here is exactly what it is for, and what it is not for.

is.explain: Explains general health information in plain language, in English, French and Arabic, using only passages from a licence-checked library of public health sources, with dated citations.
is.navigate: Helps you find your way around the hospital: departments, opening hours, contacts, directions, visiting rules and an appointment request form whose contents go to staff, never to the AI.
is.care: Points you to the right level of care. Every medical answer includes general guidance on when to seek care, and emergency or crisis messages bring up the hospital’s verified emergency contacts first.

isNot.diagnosis: Not a diagnostic tool. It does not name what you have, rank possible conditions or estimate likelihoods.
isNot.triage: Not a triage service. It does not decide how urgent your situation is.
isNot.prescriber: Not a prescriber. It does not give personal doses or advise starting, stopping or changing a treatment.
isNot.clinician: Not a substitute for a clinician, and not for use in clinical practice.

About.why: Software that gives individual medical advice is regulated as a medical device, and the AI model behind Ausculta may not be used to provide medical advice. Keeping Ausculta to general information and navigation keeps it safe and honest about what it is. You are always told that you are talking to an AI.
About.privacy: Names, phone numbers and other identifiers are removed before your message is processed or logged. Conversation text is not stored by default. Appointment requests are kept for hospital staff for 30 days.
About.demo: This is a demonstration. Hospital details are fictional, and Ausculta must not be used with real patients until a legal, clinical and privacy review is signed.
About.contact: For anything about your own health, talk to a doctor, nurse or pharmacist. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
